samples.identification: MIPS32 little-endian statically linked UDP heartbeat client
evidence: Entry at 0x4007c0 passes main at 0x4005f8 to glibc. Main is 448 bytes; the remaining functions are static runtime code.
main: fork at 0x400640, setsid at 0x400654, second fork at 0x400664; parents exit.
socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0) at 0x4006a8 connects to 45.153.34.235:10019. MIPS SOCK_DGRAM is 2.
Sends HELLO including its terminator, then sleeps 10 seconds and sends PING including its terminator. recv(..., MSG_DONTWAIT) reads at most 1023 bytes and only terminates the buffer.
Received bytes never reach a dispatcher, command execution, staging, or attack routine. Failed sends close the socket, sleep five seconds and reconnect.
No encrypted application configuration or executable content was recovered; wide-string results are incidental runtime data.
samples.source_label_explanation: Mirai attribution is not supported by the executable. A daemonized client, IoT architecture suffix, or shared collection/infrastructure context may explain the external label; these do not demonstrate hostile behavior.
samples.dependencies: Statically linked glibc; its embedded Launchpad URL was fetched and is the ordinary Ubuntu glibc bug list. The program does not download code from it.

samples.identification: SNOWLIGHT Linux x64 raw-TCP anonymous-file loader
evidence: main at 0x400950 exits when /tmp/log_de.log exists; this is an activation guard, not evidence of logging or persistence.
Connects to 124.222.150.13:8084, retrying every 10 seconds. Sends the six-byte l64 architecture tag, two network-port bytes, and 32 bytes of endpoint storage.
syscall(319, "a", 0) at 0x400a7a-0x400a88 creates a memfd through libc syscall; no memfd_create import is present.
recv at 0x400aac fills a 4096-byte buffer. The loop at 0x400abd-0x400ac9 XORs each received byte with 0x99; write at 0x400ad4 appends the transformed bytes to the same memfd.

After EOF, clears the buffer, closes the socket, resolves its original executable path into the CWD environment variable, and calls fexecve on the memfd at 0x400b37. The new argv[0] is [kworker/0:2], impersonating a kernel worker.

The socket-to-decoder-to-memfd-to-execution path and deliberate process impersonation establish hostility independently of external family labels. No stage was supplied with this specimen, and no claim is made about the downloaded stage.

samples.identification: XMRig 6.26.0 custom static PIE i386 build
evidence: Recovered main at 0x10cc0 constructs Process(argc, argv), checks Entry::get at 0x59210, dispatches help/version through Entry::exec, otherwise constructs App at 0xf5de0 and calls App::exec at 0xf5a10. This matches upstream src/xmrig.cpp.

Configuration loader around 0x4eae0-0x4ec54 tries config.json in the data location, then .xmrig.json and .config/xmrig.json in the home location. It then returns without an embedded-config fallback, matching upstream BasePrivate::load with embedded configuration disabled.
App::exec emits the configuration-wizard error at 0xf5b80 and returns 2 if controller initialization fails. On success it starts the controller and enters the libuv event loop.
JSON-RPC login construction at 0x64b8d and submit handling, RandomX/CryptoNight algorithm tables and worker configuration match the disclosed mining purpose.

Read-only strings and initializer routines contain normal algorithm/configuration registration. No forced wallet, custom pool, startup installer, credential theft, or staged executable was identified. Developer donation endpoint is donate.v2.xmrig.com.
Decoded facts include a numeric stack string, a mistaken percent-decoding of the date format, and Base64-compatible library tokens; none is executable source, an endpoint, or an additional payload.
samples.source_label_explanation: Miner/riskware detections identify its legitimate mining capability. A miner may be deployed without consent by an external installer, but this binary provides no evidence of unauthorized deployment or operation.
samples.dependencies: Static runtime, libuv, JSON and HTTP parsing code were reviewed in the mining/application paths. Referenced XMRig documentation and wizard URLs, and the GCC bug-report URL, were fetched; these are documentation/error-message references, not payload dependencies.
samples.limitation: Official release assets contain no Linux i386 build, so this is a source/behavior comparison, not a claim of byte identity with an official release.

changes: Add x64 zero-flag memfd argument recognition, requiring the syscall wrapper import for the complete capability. Remove inherited process-injection mappings from memory-file creation; creation alone is not injection.
Extend the ELF XOR loop matcher to the cursor-minus-base comparison form, with a nonzero key and full backward branch.
Place the anonymous-file execution API co-occurrence profile under process/create/exec rather than deployment; APIs alone do not establish a linked deployment chain. Update its consumers.
Move connection-status strings from state-connect to connect. Both benign static binaries remain free of suspicious/hostile findings after the move.

During the exec-directory budget audit, relocate the awk system command matcher to shell/command-string. Preserve its exact consumer and add the explicit relocated reference to the shell-capable CI relay consumer. Other exec-directory consumers either exclude shell files or already include the shell subtree.

verification.atomscan: All three targets rescanned with CLEAVE_TRAITS_DIR set to this checkout and --no-update --mode slow. The hostile sample gives exit status 1 as expected.
verification.regression_controls: Nine static mutations passed in check.py: original, different key, different endpoint, missing XOR back edge, zero XOR key, different syscall number, missing recv, missing fexecve, missing syscall wrapper. None was executed.
verification.relocation_controls: Awk command with system() matched; awk print of system-status text did not. Source matchers and severities were preserved during relocation.
